reason: The desktop runner store's writes are socket and queue bookkeeping: which socket holds an installation, run leases and states the desktop reports, queued commands and acknowledged run messages, idle installations evicted at the account cap, runners released when their credential is revoked (the revocation records its own audit event), abandoned runs ended and ended runs deleted past their retention window. Each write function carries one directive; the work a run does is audited by the caller that starts it.
